For, indeed, his dwelling-house on the Velia was somewhat imposing in appearance, hanging over the forum, and overlooking all transactions there; the access to it was hard, and to see him far off coming down, a stately and royal spectacle.

A strong constitution, alone, cannot guarantee the success of a society, even if it is essential to it. The constitution has to be respected, by citizens and government alike. Perhaps the largest lesson of empire is this: when a society is held together by no values beyond knee-jerk loyalty to the government, there is no reason to fight for the government when it comes under serious threat.
